permission.description: Allows commands::display::list_monitors (FR-101), the only app-defined command this application registers today. THE EXISTENCE OF THIS DIRECTORY IS THE SWITCH: tauri_build::build() globs permissions/**/* with no build-script change of ours, and from the first permission it finds, has_app_acl_manifest is true (tauri 2.11.5, webview/mod.rs:1823) and every APP-DEFINED command no capability names is rejected at invoke time with 'Command {} not allowed by ACL' (:1850). Two narrowings that used to be written here as absolutes, both kept short because src-tauri/src/commands/mod.rs states them in full. (1) Not every command: the same condition at :1823-1826 ends '&& request.cmd != FETCH_CHANNEL_DATA_COMMAND', so plugin:__TAURI_CHANNEL__|fetch is exempt from the ACL by construction; that costs nothing while this application creates no Channel, and the first item that creates one owns it. (2) Fail-closed, and reopening it takes a rebuild rather than being impossible: dynamic-acl is deliberately off (ADR-0013), which removes Manager::add_capability and nothing else, while Context::runtime_authority_mut and RuntimeAuthority::__allow_command stay pub and the latter grants windows:["*"]. Reaching them takes Rust code in this crate, so it takes a diff, and scripts/check-command-inventory.js makes that diff red — by grepping src-tauri/src/ for those two names with // comments removed, which catches what lands in this crate and is not a compiler: not an alias, not a macro, not a re-export, not another crate. A command registered in generate_handler! but not named by a capability is dead until the next build. scripts/check-command-inventory.js is what turns that into a red gate before a build ever runs. Conventions this file sets, and the next one should follow: one file per command, named after the command; identifier allow-<command with underscores replaced by hyphens>; commands.allow naming the command exactly as generate_handler! spells it — the same shape Tauri's own autogenerate_command_permissions writes, so a reader who knows Tauri recognises it. No deny-list-monitors counterpart is written: nothing references one, and permissions are added by the item whose FR needs them, never in anticipation. Granting this changes nothing about what the command does; it decides which windows may call it. capabilities/main-window.json grants it to 'main' alone, and capabilities/output-window.json grants this and every other app-defined command to nothing.
